headlines.title: Constellation Energy Stock Jumps. What a Google Nuclear Deal Will Do for It.
headlines.summary: Big Tech is going nuclear as Alphabet and others scramble for enough power for their AI data centers.

headlines.title: Google signs $4.3 billion nuclear power deal with Constellation
headlines.summary: The agreement will add 890 megawatts of new capacity to the PJM grid through upgrades at 11 nuclear plants in 3 states

headlines.title: Google Nears $1 Billion-Plus Nuclear Power Agreement With Constellation, Bloomberg Reports
headlines.summary: Google parent Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) is nearing an agreement to purchase nuclear power from Constellation Energy (NASDAQ:CEG) under a multi-year contract potentially worth at least $1 billion, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. The agreement could be announced as soon as this week, according to people familiar with the discussions cited by Bloomberg.

headlines.title: Google, Constellation near $1 billion-plus nuclear power deal, Bloomberg reports
headlines.summary: Investing.com -- Google parent Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is nearing an agreement to buy nuclear energy from Constellation Energy as technology companies race to secure reliable power for a rapidly expanding data-center industry, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday.

headlines.title: Why Is CEG Stock Surging More Than 4% In Overnight Trading?
headlines.summary: According to a report from Bloomberg, Google's parent company, Alphabet, is close to an agreement to buy nuclear energy from Constellation Energy in a multi-year deal valued at $1 billion, expected to be announced as soon as this week.

description: Constellation Energy Corporation produces and sells energy products and services in the United States. The company operates through five segments: Mid-Atlantic, Midwest, New York, ERCOT, and Other Power Regions. It offers electricity, natural gas, energy-related products, and sustainable solutions. The company has approximately 31,676 megawatts of generating capacity consisting of nuclear, wind, solar, natural gas, and hydroelectric assets. It serves distribution utilities, municipalities, cooperatives, and commercial, industrial, public sector, and residential customers. The company was incorporated in 2021 and is headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland.
